description: UniFi network telemetry via UnPoller. Alerting here is deliberately limited to infrastructure absence, WAN health and collector liveness — the Home Assistant UniFi integration already covers firmware, device health and client presence.

panels.title: Controller poll
panels.description: Whether UnPoller's last background poll of the controller succeeded. If this is FAILING, every panel below is stale and the absence alerts cannot be trusted.

panels.title: Metrics cache age
panels.description: Seconds since UnPoller last refreshed its cache from the controller. /metrics serves this cache, so a rising value means the data on this dashboard is old even though scrapes succeed.

panels.title: Adopted devices
panels.description: Devices adopted by the controller on the LAN subsystem.

panels.title: Disconnected
panels.description: Adopted devices the controller cannot reach. No alert fires on this — the Home Assistant UniFi integration already tracks device presence and notifies.

panels.title: Pending adoption
panels.description: Devices visible to the controller but not adopted.

panels.title: Clients
panels.description: Distinct client MACs currently reporting. This is the series set the infrastructure absence alert watches.

panels.title: WAN uptime
panels.description: Alerts UnifiWANDown below 95% for 15m. Home Assistant has no WAN status entity, so this is the only WAN health signal.

panels.title: WAN drops (24h)
panels.description: WAN disconnections in the last 24h. Metric name carries an upstream typo (intenet).

panels.title: Infrastructure client uptime
panels.description: Uptime of each MAC in UNIFI_INFRA_MACS. A line that ends and does not resume is the UnifiInfraClientAbsent condition: UnPoller emits no last_seen metric and no presence gauge, so a vanished client simply stops producing series. A switch failed this way on 2025-10-18 and went unnoticed for 11 months.

panels.title: Infrastructure clients — last seen
panels.description: Seconds since each tracked MAC last produced a sample, over a 7-day lookback. Anything above ~120s is not reporting right now; above 3600s the alert has fired.

panels.title: Gateway memory utilisation
panels.description: The 2026-09-12 audit found the gateway at 91.1% with no history to say whether that was normal. No alert rule here — the Home Assistant UniFi integration already exposes a memory utilisation sensor per device and notifies on it. This panel supplies the trend that was missing.

panels.title: Internet latency
panels.description: Controller-measured latency to the internet. Home Assistant exposes nothing equivalent.

panels.title: WAN disconnections
panels.description: Alerts UnifiWANDrops on any increase, sustained 5m.

panels.title: Devices
panels.description: Adopted device inventory with uptime and firmware version. Firmware currency is not alerted on here — Home Assistant's UniFi integration provides update entities per device and already notifies.

panels.title: Clients per AP radio
panels.description: User stations associated per AP radio.

panels.title: Channel utilisation
panels.description: Total channel utilisation per radio, including other people's networks. A 5 GHz channel swap during the audit had to be judged from two instantaneous readings because no time series existed. No alert — thresholds get set in PR 2 from a week of observed data, not a guess.

panels.title: AP transmit retry rate
panels.description: Retries as a share of transmitted packets. Single samples during the audit swung 3.4%-18.4% on one radio within an hour, which is why no alert threshold is set yet — PR 2 sets it from the observed p95 over a week. Home Assistant has no retry-rate data at all, so this is genuinely new signal.

panels.title: VAP transmit retries
panels.description: Per-virtual-AP retry rate, broken out by SSID and radio.

panels.title: Client signal strength
panels.description: Per-client signal. Filter with the Client variable — showing every client at once is unreadable on a busy site.

list.description: Device types treated as the gateway. UnPoller reports the UXG Fiber as uxg.
list.label: Gateway type
list.name: gw_type

list.description: Regex of infrastructure MACs that must never vanish. Defaults to .* so the panels are not empty; paste the UNIFI_INFRA_MACS value to scope them.
list.label: Infra MACs
list.name: infra_macs
